svg.data-fans: 4x hot-swappable 3+1 redundant, exhaust airflow; system front-to-back
svg.data-cpu: Intel Icelake-D 8-core @ 2.1 GHz (Standard) or Icelake-D 16-core @ 2.0 GHz (Premium), with VROC support
svg.data-oem-alias: DriveNets NCP-96X6C-S (Network Cloud Packet forwarder, 96x1/10/25 + 6x100). NOT A UFISPACE CLAIM - no UfiSpace document mentions DriveNets. The mapping is internal analysis matching DriveNets' NCP-96X6C-S (Q2C 2.4T) to this chassis on published silicon and port configuration. The map names the S9600-102XC OR this Ice Lake refresh for the same DriveNets name, so the alias is not unique to one of the pair. Recorded so a search for either name finds this box; no DriveNets figure or artwork is transcribed anywhere in this file.
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO, ITU-T SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 (G.8265.1 default, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 with additional licence; T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC), Time Sensitive Networking, Class C accuracy
svg.data-timing-interfaces: GNSS SMA in, 1PPS SMB in/out, 10MHz SMB in/out, ToD RJ45 in/out
svg.data-gnss: internal receiver for master clock implementations
svg.data-timing-cables: 50 ohm SMA coax with 1/4-36UNS-2B for GNSS; 50 ohm SMB coax with 10-32UNF-2A for 1PPS and 10MHz; shielded RJ45 for ToD
svg.data-nos: NOS integration is necessary to activate the timing features
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 25G SFP28 SR, LR, ER; 10G SFP+ SR, LR, ER; 1G SFP SX, LX, EX (datasheet Compatible Transceivers Types)
svg.data-optics-qsfp28: 100G QSFP28 SR4, LR4, ER4, ZR4 (datasheet Compatible Transceivers Types)
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: 10G SFP+ SR, LR, ER (datasheet Compatible Transceivers Types; the two 10G management ports take the same optics as the SFP28 cages do at 10G)
svg.data-reset: recessed front-panel pinhole, warm-resets the host CPU when held for less than 10 seconds; HIG section 4.5 warns against sharp tools and asks for the UfiSpace fixture or a flat paperclip
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 55035; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI

Everything else in the two products' documents agrees (same 436 x 609.6 x 87.7 chassis, same port counts and numbering, same FRU tables, same LED table), so the faceplate is very likely genuinely unchanged and the badge is the only thing known to be wrong; the model badge here is drawn 'S9601-102XC'. That is an inference across the panel from one block, and if it is wrong it is wrong for forty-eight ports at once.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["sfp28"],"wanted":"a straight-on high-resolution front photograph, or a vendor 3D model","what":"sfp-traffic-row-mirroring"},{"note":"Both QSFP28 blocks sit against an olive-green perforated plate carrying two rows of round holes and one bright vertical clip per cage column. Not one row in this guide's tables is annotated 'need NOS to activate' as the S9510-28DC's are, so there is no evidence either way about whether these are NOS-defined.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["sfp28","qsfp28","sfp-plus-mgmt","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"The only rear elevation in the intake is a three-quarter render whose face is 2.5% anisotropic (3.796 px/mm across, 3.988 down) and whose left-hand body edge cannot be separated from the skew of its own top surface to better than a couple of millimetres, so the figure alone cannot place a feature better than that. What settles the rear is the PHOTOGRAPH; legends beside the supplies are resolved on it and are drawn.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"an orthographic rear elevation or a mechanical drawing","what":"rear-face-geometry"},{"note":"ufispace/fan-803816-hi states no draw and its own contract records the search. L29's standing warning is the live count of how much of the chassis total is a floor. On a box with four fans in a 2RU 102-port chassis this is a material hole, not a rounding one.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ufispace/fan-803816-hi@1"],"wanted":"a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet","what":"fru-power-unpublished"},{"note":"The datasheet's Processor row offers 'Intel Icelake-D 8-Core @ 2.1GHz (Standard)' and 'Intel Icelake-D 16-Core @ 2.0GHz (Premium)' without naming a default, and no orderable SKU distinguishes them anywhere in the intake. Both are carried in one attr rather than one being chosen. Four media, one job; the three coaxial jacks run along the top of the faceplate and the ToD jack sits below them","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9601-102XC","name":"s9601-102xc","portfolio":{"family":"Open Aggregation Router","line":"Telecoms","series":"S9600 Series"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"attrs":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet (Specifications / Performance / Regulatory Compliance / Supported Accessories) and HIG (the Port Overview table for reach and speed, section 11 for the console settings, section 4.5 for the reset button). THE PROCESSOR ROW CARRIES TWO SKUS - 'Intel Icelake-D 8-Core @ 2.1GHz (Standard)' and 'Intel Icelake-D 16-Core @ 2.0GHz (Premium)', plus 'VROC Support' - and both are transcribed rather than one being chosen, because the datasheet offers them as alternatives and names no default. Compliance transcribed as printed and not tidied - note that this datasheet lists BSMI under EMC where the sibling's does not, and puts ETSI 300 019 and ETSI 300 132-2 under Environment beside WEEE, which are an environmental-conditions and a power-interface standard rather than a materials one; they are carried where the vendor put them."},"bottom":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"estimated - no source in the intake shows the underside. The compliance sticker is the house convention at an estimated position. A bottom view mirrors LEFT and RIGHT; the sticker is the only content, so the axis was checked and does not bite."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet '2 RU, 436 x 609 x 87.7 mm', 'Weight withou FRU: 15.19kg' (the vendor's typo), with the HIG Component Physical Information table giving the depth to a decimal - 'S9601-102XC (W x D x H) 17.16 x 24 x 3.45 in (436 x 609.6 x 87.7mm)' - and the same weight ('Chassis without FRU 33.49lb (15.19kg)'). 436 IS THE BODY, NOT THE RACK FACE: the HIG Space Clearance paragraph says 'The S9601-102XC width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks'. The brackets are visible in Figure 8 as tabs beyond both ends of the face and are not drawn. Depth 609.6 is 'without the field replaceable units'; the same paragraph adds that the fan handle stands 29 mm proud and the PSU handle 30 mm, and that 6 inches of clearance front and rear are needed."},"colour":{"note":"photo and drawing - the faceplate is near-black, not the slate the renderer defaults to. Both the vendor's front photograph and Figure 8's own artwork put the metal at a luminance around 40 of 255 against the port shells' 230, so chassis.color is set to '#23272b'. NOTE THAT THIS DEPARTS FROM THE REST OF THE UFISPACE SET, which leaves the colour unset and therefore renders slate; the departure is deliberate and follows the two sources rather than the house default, and the other files should probably follow."},"front-figure-scale":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - HIG page 11, the Figure 8 port-overview elevation, re-rendered at 600 dpi. GATE 1: at a luminance threshold that takes the panel border and not its antialiasing, the drawn faceplate measures 3748 x 754 px (x 831-4578, y 1735-2488), which is 8.5963 px/mm against 436 mm and 8.5975 px/mm against 87.7 mm - 0.01% apart. The figure is orthographic and every front coordinate below is measured on it at 8.5969 px/mm from the panel's top-left corner. THE THRESHOLD IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT: at a looser one the same box reads 3754 x 761 and the two scales fall 0.78% apart, which would still pass but by luck. The rack-mount ear tabs stick out past both ends and are excluded; they are not metal between the ear folds."},"fru-components":{"note":"reuses ufispace/psu-132-ac, ufispace/psu-132-dc and ufispace/fan-803816-hi. The fan match is nominal AND dimensional: this datasheet's ordering line is FAN-803816-HI and that component carries exactly that part number, which is a better fit than the sibling's choice of fan-808012 with a per-configuration model override. The two contracts' own part numbers for the supplies differ from this datasheet's - PSU-132-AISB1/DISB1 against PSU-132-AESR/DESR - which is a suffix naming the airflow and the chassis family rather than a different face, so the per-device numbers are carried in the configurations' component-attrs where a FRU model belongs. THE TWO VENDOR TABLES ROUND THE FAN DIFFERENTLY: this HIG's Component Physical Information gives 'Fan (W x D x H) 3.2 x 4.8 x 3.19 in (81 x 113 x 81.5mm)' while fan-803816-hi's own source, the S9600-28DX HIG, gives 80 x 113 x 81.5 for the same part number. That is a millimetre of rounding, not a disagreement worth a gap entry; the bays are drawn at the component's 80.0 so the module fills its opening exactly rather than leaving a dark sliver, and the 81 is recorded here."},"led-semantics":{"note":"HIG section 10, pages 22-23 of the converted text, transcribed rather than only cited. Six system lamps - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID - with the two supplies getting a lamp each rather than sharing one PWR lamp, SYS carrying only three rows and no blinking green, and an ID beacon whose only documented state is Blinking Blue. The PSU FRU and Fan FRU tables belong to the modules and are transcribed in ufispace/psu-132-ac, psu-132-dc and fan-803816-hi."},"left":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"estimated - no figure or photograph in the intake resolves a flank, and the top view shows only the fold line. Perimeter screws at estimated positions; the face is honestly sparse rather than blank. AXIS: x = 0 is the REAR on a left view (viewer3d.js convention). This face carries only symmetric content, which is recorded so that the axis reads as checked rather than as not having mattered."},"lifecycle":{"note":"searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S9601-102XC end of life end of sale' - no announcement found; the product is current and the guide is dated August 2026. none-announced is a real finding, not an omission."},"mgmt-cluster":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured off a 2.2x crop of the left service area. One silver bezel at about x 21.6-38.3, y 48.6-80.4 holding three things in a column: the out-of-band RJ45 (drawn face 49.6-59.8, green link lamps in its TOP corners so it is keyway-up, rotate 180), a USB 3.0 Type-A socket with the blue tongue the datasheet's '1 x USB 3.0 Type-A port' implies (61.3-67.1), and the RS-232 console RJ45 keyway-down at 68.7-80.4, labelled IOIOI below - the HIG's own spelling, 'The console can be connected with the IOIO port'. Both RJ45s are std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11): the bezel is 17.3 wide and 32.0 tall, which will not take two 16 x 14 IEC cutouts and a USB. Three icons are printed above the bezel at y 44.7-46.5 - a network glyph centred 22.6, an up/down pair centred 28.3, and the USB SuperSpeed trident centred 34.8. The icon PATH GEOMETRY is the sibling's, redrawn at my own measured centres; the glyphs are 2 mm wide and my render does not resolve their strokes. The recessed RESET button is centred (13.9, 45.9) and about 2.4 mm across, drawn with common/reset-button at its own 4.0 contract size because nothing smaller exists."},"mgmt-sfp-plus":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - the two 10G SFP+ management ports are a one-column, two-row ganged block of their own, shell x 25.36-41.06, with their own up/down lamp pair in the land and their own printed '0 up down 1' legend above. Their apertures are drawn OPEN, unlike the traffic blocks': measured on four columns clear of the central latch tab, the upper opening spans y 16.52-24.54 and the lower 32.22-40.36, centres 20.53 and 36.29, so the 10.4 mm cages sit at 15.33 and 31.09 - about 0.4 above the traffic rows, which is what the drawing says. Cage x 26.09, the shell's centre. The vendor numbers them 0 and 1 in their own sequence, which is why they are a separate group: the traffic ports also start at 0."},"part-numbers":{"note":"none stated for the chassis. Neither the datasheet nor the HIG prints an orderable chassis SKU; the datasheet's 'Available to Order' section names only the supplies (PSU-132-DESR 1300W DC exhaust, PSU-132-AESR 1300W AC exhaust) and the fan (FAN-803816-HI, exhaust air flow). No SKU is invented, so the configurations carry none - the same finding, and the same treatment, as the other UfiSpace boxes here."},"port-pitch":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured, FROM A FEATURE THAT REPEATS ONCE PER PORT rather than from the filled rectangles the figure draws for the seated modules. Averaging rows 18-24 mm and 48-54 mm and taking the bright cage separators gives, in the upper-left block, boundaries at 57.70 ... 200.19 mm - ten intervals, (200.19-57.70)/10 = 14.249 - and in the lower-left block 58.16 ... 200.60, (200.60-58.16)/10 = 14.244. The two right-hand blocks give eleven intervals each with a mean of 14.25 and 14.27. Four independent runs, one per block, all within 0.03 of 14.25 mm, which is exactly std/sfp-ganged's contract width (SFF-8433 port pitch B04), so the standard part fits with no gutter and no drift across twelve columns."},"power":{"note":"one figure, one measure, and its scope is stated. Datasheet Power Supply block: 'Typical power: 399 Watts (no transceiver)' - a typical, explicitly with the cages empty, which on a 102-port box is a large qualifier. THIS IS 20 W ABOVE THE S9600-102XC's 379 W and that is a real difference between two products, not two readings: the S9601 carries an Icelake-D host against the S9600's Skylake-D, twice the memory and two SSDs against one. The HIG states no system consumption figure at all; its only wattage is the provisioning instruction on each power circuit, which is the PSU rating and not a draw, and is not recorded as one. NO MAXIMUM IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE IN THE INTAKE - searched both documents for 'watt', 'W)' and 'consumption' - so none is invented and power-envelope is 'bare', the one qualifier the single figure does declare. PSU inputs from the datasheet (AC 100-240 V 12 A, DC -40 to -75 V 40 A), corroborated by the HIG's Preparation Check List; the per-PSU rating lives on the ufispace/psu-132-* contracts."},"qsfp28":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - six QSFP28 in TWO blocks, not one: a two-column pair whose shell runs x 391.65-430.39 carrying 96/98 on the top row and 97/99 on the bottom, and a single column, shell 391.65-411.31, carrying 100 over 101. Cage columns at 392.30 and 411.30, a 19.0 mm pitch against std/qsfp-ganged's 18.5 contract width, so the two cages do not abut; the column positions are the sibling's reading of this artwork and my shell measurements bracket them to a few tenths at both ends. The QSFP rows are CENTRED ON THE SFP ROWS rather than aligned to their tops - a taller port on the same centreline - so each 9.58 mm cage sits 0.41 above its SFP neighbour's 10.4 mm one, at y 16.26, 31.71, 46.31 and 61.51. Top rows are rotated 180 for the same reason the SFP top rows are."},"qsfp28-lamps":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - the land between each QSFP pair carries a dense dot matrix rather than the SFP blocks' two arrows: four lamps per port, drawn with ufispace/lane-led-quad (14.4 x 2.6, four round lamps on a 3.94 pitch, built for exactly this vendor's QSFP28 blocks). One strip per port, stacked in the land at y 26.0 and 28.8 (upper block) and 55.9 and 58.7 (lower). g.data-description: led-mgmt-l: the management jack's left corner lamp, drawn lit green in HIG Figure 8. THE HIG TABLES NO MANAGEMENT-PORT LED for this platform - the S9510-28DC and M3000-14XC guides do and this one does not - so the states here are the component default and not a transcription; led-mgmt-r: the management jack's right corner lamp; same absence of a vendor table as its left-hand twin, and the same component default
g.title: mgmt

g.data-description: HIG SYNC row - OFF (timing synchronization disabled or free-run), Solid Green (timing core synchronized to PTP phase or one of the external timing sources and frequency also locked), Blinking Green (synchronized to a PTP frequency profile or an external SyncE source), Solid Amber (acquiring or holdover), Blinking Amber (synchronization fail, or acquiring/holdover timed out)
g.title: led-sync

g.data-description: HIG SYS row - OFF (no power), Solid Green (host CPU/BMC boot complete), Solid Amber (power is up but host CPU/BMC boot failed). Three rows only: this table gives SYS no blinking state
g.title: led-sys

g.data-description: HIG FAN row - OFF (fan modules not initialized), Solid Green (all fan modules working normally), Blinking Amber (fan fail: one or more fans need service)
g.title: led-fan

g.data-description: HIG PS0 row - OFF (no power), Solid Green (PSU0 working normally), Blinking Amber (PSU0 fail, PSU0 needs service). This platform gives each supply its own lamp rather than sharing one PWR lamp
g.title: led-ps0

g.data-description: HIG PS1 row - OFF (no power), Solid Green (PSU1 working normally), Blinking Amber (PSU1 fail, PSU1 needs service)
g.title: led-ps1

g.data-description: HIG ID row - OFF (no power), Blinking Blue (enable beacon feature). Two rows, and the blue is the only colour this lamp is documented to show
g.title: led-id

g.data-description: the pair the datasheet calls '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports', printed 0 and 1 in their own sequence above their own two-row block
